source_title: Naderi breaks Aberdeen’s resistance as Rangers reach Premier Sports Cup final
source_excerpt:
Ryan Naderi’s dramatic late strike broke down Aberdeen’s stubborn resistance to earn Rangers a place in the Premier Sports Cup final.
Aberdeen restricted Rangers to one shot on target in a low quality first half, but Derek McInnes’s side picked up the pace after the break. Aberdeen survived relentless pressure at times but in the 83rd minute Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net for his eighth goal of the season to seal a 1-0 win at Hampden Park.
The 23-year-old Naderi later tried to share the glory, saying: “It feels amazing. I’m happy, of course, happy to be the one who scores the goals, but happy for the team. I think we deserved it. We believed we could score right up until the very end and we did, and I think it’s a deserved win.”
It was another close-range strike from Naderi and he joked about this proficiency from distance. The Germany-born Czechia international said: “I’ve tried to shoot twice today from outside of the box and it didn’t go well.
“So I went back inside the box. Maybe I should just stick to the easy ones! As I said, I’m just happy how it is right now and I’m going to try to stick to it.”
Rangers – who will face the winners of Sunday’s semi-final between Hearts and Hibernian in the final – went into the game unbeaten in 10 and firm favourites.
With five Aberdeen defenders missing through suspension or injury – Lewis Mayo, Mats Knoester, Dan Happe, Kristers Tobers and Chris Cadden – there was a makeshift element about their lineup, with a first start of the season for Nicky Devlin.
McInnes, the Rangers manager who won the trophy with Aberdeen in 2014, raised eyebrows by dropping midfielder Dan Neil, with left-back Tuur Rommens starting and Penrice moving into midfield, and Badredine Bouanani starting in place of Djeidi Gassama.
There was more readjustment for Aberdeen when Emmanuel Gyamfi injured himself trying to tackle Kim Min-su and was replaced by Stuart Armstrong.
In the 23rd minute, the Rangers defence parted and Nesta Guinness-Walker drove through the gap, forcing goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to save. Aberdeen captain Kevin Nisbet glanced a header wide of the goal before Naderi hooked an effort over the crossbar.
Simo Valakari dedicated St Johnstone ’s battling 2-2 draw at Kilmarnock to the goalkeeper Toby Steward, who was dismissed in the 14th minute (pictured) after misjudging a long ball and handling outside his penalty area. Saints then twice fell behind to Cathal McCarthy and Djenairo Daniels, but equalised both times with goals from Danny Schmidt and Joel Cotterill to capture an unlikely point. The substitute goalkeeper Ross Sinclair, who came on at the expense of Taylor Steven, also made multiple second-half saves to help Saints move up to seventh.
Valakari, the St Johnstone manager, said: “Toby has held his hands up and said: ‘I am sorry, boys, for what I did.’ But our team did it for Toby, the boys did it for Taylor, who I needed to take out straight away.
“We are all here playing for each other. We have got each other’s backs when things happen. That tells me my players are ready to accept any responsibility. Early red card, with Toby that’s my tactical choice. I ask my keeper to play very high, like a sweeper-keeper for those long balls. In those moments, for a year, Toby has been fantastic in clearing the ball, reading the ball. It’s a thin line, a little outside the box, that can happen.”
Alfred Johansson admitted he was left to sweat as Motherwell broke a seven-game winless run with a 1-0 win over St Mirren . Lukas Fadinger rattled home a penalty eight minutes from time to relieve some pressure on the Swede as the Fir Park side climbed into eighth.
Johansson was adamant his team were well worthy of a result, which brought welcome relief to both him and his players. He said: “Even more than relief, I felt good, happy, joy, determination. This group has done really well lately and I think it’s very well deserved to get the victory and have at least four points from these last two games. It’s important to build on it, the most important thing today is that we didn’t give away easy goals or big chances at all." Press Association
Just before the break Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Müller parried a low drive from Bouanani to safety, then Naderi headed a cross from stand-in captain Nico Raskin just over before Kim slashed a drive wide.
As the game became stretched, Pandur saved a deflected Kevin Nesbit drive then Müller blocked a shot from Kim before Rangers striker Kevin Kelsy somehow managed to head a pinpoint delivery from Bouanani past a post from six yards.
Müller’s foot blocked another effort from Bouanani and beat away a Raskin volley as the Aberdeen box came under siege. On a rare break, Nesbit’s shot was deflected wide and from the corner the Aberdeen striker hooked over the bar.
Aberdeen finally succumbed when Bouanani knocked the ball back to Penrice and he fired towards goal, with Naderi stepping in to beat Müller from close range.

## रेन्जर्स की संघर्षपूर्ण जीत

रयान नदेरी के मैच के अंतिम क्षणों में किए गए महत्वपूर्ण गोल की बदौलत रेन्जर्स ने एबरडीन को 1-0 से हराकर प्रीमियर स्पोर्ट्स कप के फाइनल में प्रवेश कर लिया है। हैम्पडन पार्क में खेले गए इस मुकाबले में एबरडीन की मजबूत रक्षात्मक पंक्ति ने रेन्जर्स को लंबे समय तक रोके रखा, लेकिन अंततः मैच का फैसला हुआ।

## मैच के मुख्य आकर्षण

* **निर्णायक गोल:** मैच के 83वें मिनट में जेम्स पेन्रिस के शॉट को रयान नदेरी ने गोल में बदलकर अपनी टीम को बढ़त दिलाई। यह उनका इस सीजन का आठवां गोल था।
* **कड़ा मुकाबला:** पहले हाफ में दोनों टीमों के बीच कड़ा संघर्ष देखने को मिला, जहाँ एबरडीन ने रेन्जर्स को ज्यादा मौके नहीं दिए।
* **दूसरा हाफ:** ब्रेक के बाद दोनों टीमों ने आक्रामक खेल दिखाया, जिसमें रेन्जर्स ने लगातार दबाव बनाए रखा।

## खिलाड़ियों और प्रबंधकों की प्रतिक्रिया

मैच के बाद 23 वर्षीय नदेरी ने अपनी टीम के प्रदर्शन की सराहना करते हुए कहा कि अंत तक विश्वास बनाए रखने के कारण उन्हें यह जीत मिली। इस जीत के साथ रेन्जर्स अब फाइनल में पहुँच गई है, जहाँ उनका मुकाबला संडे को होने वाले हार्ट्स और हिबर्नियन के बीच सेमीफाइनल के विजेता से होगा।

## आगे की जानकारी कैसे सत्यापित करें

इस मैच से जुड़ी आधिकारिक घोषणाओं और स्कोर की पुष्टि के लिए संबंधित लीग के आधिकारिक खेल पोर्टल या खेल समाचारों की अधिकृत वेबसाइट्स पर जाया जा सकता है।

## Late Breakthrough at Hampden Park

Ryan Naderi scored a dramatic late goal in the 83rd minute to secure a 1-0 victory for Rangers against Aberdeen, sending his side through to the Premier Sports Cup final at Hampden Park.

Aberdeen deployed a makeshift lineup due to five defensive players missing through suspension or injury. Despite restricting Rangers to a single shot on target in a low-quality first half, Aberdeen faced mounting pressure after the interval before finally conceding late in the match.

## Match Highlights and Tactical Shifts

* **The Decisive Goal:** In the 83rd minute, James Penrice fired toward goal, and Naderi redirected the strike past the goalkeeper for his eighth goal of the season.
* **Aberdeen Resilience:** Despite being forced into tactical adjustments and an early substitution after Emmanuel Gyamfi sustained an injury tackling Kim Min-su, Aberdeen's defense held firm under sustained pressure for much of the second half.
* **Missed Chances:** Both sides created opportunities as the game stretched, with Rangers' Kevin Kelsy heading past the post from close range and Aberdeen threatening through Kevin Nisbet.

## Post-Match Comments

Following the game, match-winner Naderi expressed delight with the result while remaining modest about his close-range scoring proficiency. 

"It feels amazing. I’m happy, of course, happy to be the one who scores the goals, but happy for the team," Naderi said. Commenting on his attempts from distance, he joked: "I’ve tried to shoot twice today from outside of the box and it didn’t go well. So I went back inside the box. Maybe I should just stick to the easy ones!"

## Next Steps

* **The Final:** Rangers will face the winners of the semi-final between Hearts and Hibernian.
